The original vision of data-to-text generation was to take complex data and describe it using natural language ...

In this paper, we propose the novel concept of data views, where all available data is divided into manageable subsets, describing entities and their attributes along one or more dimensions. Views are then aligned with corresponding spans of text. They can then be combined to form high level document plans (schema) for neural data-to-text systems, controlling the generation of text without sacrificing factual accuracy.

We performed our experiment with one annotator per text 6 . The original protocol limited annotators to only 4 prior games before defaulting to Not Checkable errors. We felt this was overly restrictive so we asked annotators to check all assertions within the current season. We compared generations for 35 random basketball games, generating a text for each of the 7 systems. A Latin square design was used whereby each participant annotated 5 texts for each system, never seeing the same game twice (245 total annotated texts).
guideline: Annotators highlight errors in text spans and categorize them into predefined error types using a protocol with reference to basketball-reference.com.

Annotators marked errors in the generated summaries and selected one of several error categories; they also answered questions about sentence positioning (remain, transpose, move short distance, move long distance).

Participants are provided with links to basketball-reference.com, which is at least as complete as the system input data, and much easier for humans to navigate. Four main error categories are used; Name (named entities), Number (ordinal, cardinal, etc), Word (a word or phrase that is not a name or number), Context (such as implicature errors). There is also the last resort category Other, for text that is nonsensical. Finally, there is a Not Checkable category, which covers facts that are impractical or impossible to check using the provided reference data.
criteria: sentence ordering (remain, transpose, short move, long move)
